# Spanish Minor 2: Language, Culture, and Professional Contexts
Source: https://academiccatalog.umd.edu/undergraduate/colleges-schools/arts-humanities/languages-literatures-cultures/spanish-language-literatures-culture/spanish-language-culture-professional-minor/

## Catalog requirements

Prerequisites: SPAN103, SPAN203, SPAN204, or equivalent.
Course | Title | Credits
SPAN207 | Reading and Writing in Spanish | 3
SPAN301 | Advanced Grammar and Composition I | 3
SPAN303 | Approaches to Cultural Materials in the Hispanic World | 3
SPAN311 | Advanced Communication I | 3
or SPAN316 | Spanish Translation I
Select one of the following: | 3
SPAN331 | Spanish Culture, Civilization and Literature I: Medieval Times
SPAN332 | Spanish Culture, Civilization and Literature II: Renaissance and Baroque
SPAN333 | Spanish Culture, Civilization and Literature III: Modern Times
SPAN361 | Latin American Literatures and Cultures I: From Pre-Columbian to Colonial Times
SPAN362 | Latin American Literatures and Cultures II: From Independence to Nation Formation
SPAN363 | Latin American Literatures and Cultures III: From Modernism to Neo-Liberalism
One 3xx or 4xx-level course in Language, Culture, and Professional Contexts: 1 | 3
SPAN318
SPAN370 | Spanish for Business I
SPAN371 | Spanish for the Health Professions
SPAN373 | Spanish in the Media
SPAN374 | Spanish in the Community
SPAN375 | Spanish in the Life Sciences
SPAN422 | Intercultural Communication and Negotiation
SPAN480 | Spanish for Business II
Total Credits | 18
1
Areas include: Translation, Business, Media, Health, Community Engagement/Education, Law, and Life Sciences.
Areas include: Translation, Business, Media, Health, Community Engagement/Education, Law, and Life Sciences.
Note: All courses must be in Spanish
Heritage learners who place out of SPAN206 can follow the sequence SPAN306 (Spanish for Heritage Speakers II) and SPAN307 (Oral Communication Skills for Heritage Speakers of Spanish).
Native speakers and all others with the ability to begin coursework at a higher level should speak with the Spanish Undergraduate Advisor for course substitutions.
It is not permitted for students to take SPAN301 and SPAN303 simultaneously; this is possible only by permission of the Spanish Undergraduate Advisor.
Two courses (up to six credits) from study abroad may apply toward the minor.

Department of Spanish & Portuguese
Home
Languages and Programs
Experience a dynamic and comprehensive education in the languages, literatures, and cultures of the Spanish and Portuguese-speaking world. Located near Washington, D.C., our program provides a unique opportunity to engage with diverse global cultures in our vibrant metropolitan area and pursue excellence in the production of new knowledge.
Undergraduate
Graduate
Special Programs
People
Lecture Series
Translation Services
Give
Undergraduate
Explore Spanish and Portuguese
Explore specialized courses in literature, culture, and professions like business, health, and law. Enhance your studies with a second major in fields such as international business or psychology, and combine language with careers in legal, health, and science sectors.
Graduate
M.A. & Ph.D. in Spanish Language & Literature
Graduates of the Spanish M.A. and Ph.D. programs are prepared to meet the demands of highly competitive positions in the United States, Latin America, the Caribbean, Portugal, and Spain.
Special Programs
Special Programs
Engage with the Spanish speaking diaspora through our Study Abroad programs or enhance your language skills at the Language House. Writers can refine their craft at the Jiménez Porter Writers House, while the Spanish Writing Center provides support for improving Spanish writing.
People
People
The Faculty of the Department of Spanish and Portuguese (SPAP) is committed to excellence in teaching and mentoring, along with the production of new knowledge that is the hallmark of a strong department.
Lecture Series
Speaker Series and Special Lectures
The Department of Spanish and Portuguese is proud to organize and host several important lecture series open to the university and the general public. Renowned intellectuals and professors from Latin America, Spain, and the American Academy have mentored many generations of our students.
Translation Services
Spanish and Portuguese Translation and Interpretation Services
Our services provide quality and reasonably priced English-Spanish/Portuguese or Spanish/Portuguese-English translations or interpretations to the University of Maryland and to other institutions, community organizations, and businesses in the Greater Washington DC area.
Give
Give to SPAP
The generous support of alumni and friends makes what we do in SPAP possible. Give today to fund real-world experiences, both local and global, and support pioneering research across disciplines that will confront the most difficult questions and problems that we face in today’s ever-changing world. Together we can make a difference!

History of the Department
The Department of Spanish and Portuguese has been the home of major Latin American and Spanish literary figures, including Juan Ramon Jimenez, as well as that of cultural critic Angel Rama, award-winning poet Jose Emilio Pacheco, renowned writer and Professors Emeriti, Jorge Aguilar Mora and Professor Emerita, Graciela Palau de Nemes.

Academics
World Language Placement (WLP) is designed to ensure that you are placed in the correct world language course based on prior coursework or exposure to a language. There is no way to fail the assessment. Please review the information below to determine which option to choose.
Online WLP
I want to take a language course or I have 2 years or fewer of language experience. Learn More
Proctored WLP
I am/will be an ARHU major and I have 3 or more years of language experience. Learn More
